newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close at 8-mth high on high liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close at 8-mth high on high liquidity.

text.p: South Korean stocks rose to their highest close in nearly eight months on Friday on buying of banks and blue chips spurred by ample liquidity, brokers said.
The composite index gained 1.87 percent or 14.49 points to 789.15 points, the highest closing since October 26, 1996, when it stood at 791.81.
Volume totalled 83.62 million shares, sharply up from Thursday's 59.66 million. Turnover also increased to 1.12 trillion won from Thursday's 874 billion.
Despite the index rise, declining stocks beat advancers by 458 to 364, while 83 stocks traded unchanged.
Brokers said construction shares sharply gained as investors thought low interest rates would help boost earnings at the construction firms that heavily rely on borrowings.
"Banks also drew attention, especially among individual investors, as the cash liquidity continued to be high," said a Daishin Securities analyst.
Second-line shares fell partly on profit-taking and partly because of news that the stock market watchdog would intensify investigations into company announcements that could influence share prices.
Blue-chip manufacturers also rose on renewed hopes for an economic recovery.
Major private research bodies said on Friday they had revised upward their forecasts for the nation's gross domestic product (GDP) growth for this year due to recovering exports.
They upgraded their forecasts to 5.5-6.2 percent from 4.7-5.7 percent, compared with last year's 7.1 percent growth.
Brokers said the market would remain upbeat next week, although strong selling pressure was seen waiting near the psychological 800-point level.
